memories.content: Define in one sentence the user groups and usage contexts to which the design knowledge does not apply.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through explicitly excluded targets and situations.
Specify user goals, interaction conditions, and technological constraints under which the proposed design knowledge can be transferred.
Small-scale formative studies can support analytic generalization distinct from statistical representativeness when results are expressed in terms of design conditions and mechanisms.
The author of this proposal tends to apply design knowledge derived from an accessible sample to a broader user population.
Keep the main text to the total and major categories, and place quantities, unit rates, and assumptions in one compact budget table or appendix.
Give each cost category, quantity, unit rate, and subtotal a stable row in the separate budget table.
Put the estimate basis in a dedicated table column so one assumption can be checked or revised without rewriting the narrative.
Readers can verify arithmetic and compare categories faster in a consistent table than in amounts distributed across prose.
Revise one table row and its subtotal when an estimate changes instead of repeating the new amount across several prose paragraphs.
Keep detailed arithmetic out of the main argument when readers can reach the complete table from a clear reference.
The user tends to interrupt the argument with long cost enumerations when no separate budget table is available.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate concerns: the reference frame defines defensible transfer and generalization boundaries for design knowledge, while the compared frame structures budget information for clarity, verification, and maintainability. Neither frame supplies a claim that substantively corresponds to one in the other.

relations.reason: Both memories express the same one-sided claim that excluded targets and contexts should be stated so the limits of generalization can be assessed.
relations.summary: Explicit exclusions identify the user groups and situations outside the design knowledge’s generalization boundary and make that boundary reviewable.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame provides operational conditions for determining where proposed design knowledge can transfer.
relations.summary: Transferability should be bounded by specified user goals, interaction conditions, and technological constraints.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame distinguishes mechanism-based analytic generalization from population-level statistical representation.
relations.summary: Small formative studies may support analytic generalization without statistical representativeness when findings identify design conditions and mechanisms.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame records this specific tendency toward overgeneralization.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to extend design knowledge from an accessible sample to a broader population.

relations.reason: Both memories state the same one-sided separation policy, with the clear-reference condition preserving access to the full detail.
relations.summary: Keep detailed budget arithmetic outside the main argument in a complete compact table or appendix reached through a clear reference, while retaining totals and major categories in the main text.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame specifies stable row-level organization for budget components.
relations.summary: Each cost category, quantity, unit rate, and subtotal should occupy a stable row in the separate budget table.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame specifies a separate structural location for each estimate basis.
relations.summary: Estimate assumptions should occupy a dedicated table column so they can be checked or revised independently of the narrative.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame states this reader-facing verification and comparison benefit.
relations.summary: A consistent budget table lets readers verify arithmetic and compare cost categories faster than prose-distributed amounts.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame specifies the maintenance procedure for changed estimates.
relations.summary: When an estimate changes, revise its table row and subtotal rather than repeating the update across multiple prose passages.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame records this specific tendency in budget presentation.
relations.summary: Without a separate budget table, the user tends to interrupt the argument with lengthy cost enumerations.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers separating budget detail from the argument, structuring estimate data, supporting verification and revision, and a tendency toward disruptive cost enumeration.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers exclusions, transfer conditions, analytic generalization, and a tendency to overextend findings from accessible samples.
